cards.explain: A moving coil instrument needs a unidirectional current, so the alternating signal is rectified before display.

cards.question: Why does an analogue vibration indicator need a filter selection at all
options: Because motor and add-on vibrations fall in different frequency ranges
Because the scale carries no units of measurement, only a trend
Because the sensor output is an alternating current, not a direct one
cards.explain: High oscillations come from the motor and low ones from the add-on components, so the filter has to be set to the range being looked at.

cards.question: The pointer of a vibration indicator sits below the zero mark, so what has happened?
options: The vibration has fallen to nothing
A system error has occurred
The filter has been switched off
cards.explain: A pointer below zero on the OFF / Error mark means a system error, not a zero vibration.

cards.question: Why does the vibration monitoring system need the tachometer signals as well as the accelerometer signals
options: Because the indicator scale must be set to the right range
Because the tracking filter must follow the rotor speed
Because the charge amplifiers must be supplied with power
cards.explain: The filter has to track the rotor speed, and it is the tachometer signals that tell it that speed.

cards.question: How can one sensor signal be turned into separate N1 and N2 vibration indications
options: By comparing its frequency with the two rotor speed signals
By switching the filter between the forward and the aft pick-up
By comparing its amplitude with the two stored limit values
cards.explain: The frequency of the vibration signal is compared with the two rotor speed signals to sort it into N1 and N2.

cards.question: A rotor speed signal is not available to the monitoring unit, so which indication mode is used?
options: BB
LPT
FAN
cards.explain: Without a rotor speed signal the filters cannot track, so the unfiltered broad band mode is used.

cards.question: Which actions may a pilot take after a vibration indication begins to pulse
options: Checking the oil pressure, closing the bleeds or re-lighting the engine
Selecting the aft pick-up, resetting the filter or changing the mode
Scanning other engine indications, reducing power or shutting down
cards.explain: The pilot has to look for the reason, by scanning other engine indications, reducing power or shutting the engine down.

cards.question: Why are the sensor and filter functions displayed beside a single vibration value
options: Because each rotor system is given its own separate indication
Because the unit picks the highest signal and its source must be known
Because the crew choose the sensor and the filter with two switches
cards.explain: With only one value shown and the unit free to pick whichever signal is highest, the crew must be told which sensor and filter produced it.

cards.question: Which three components make up the main rotor rpm monitoring system
options: A magnetic pick up, an rpm indicator and an rpm warning unit
A magnetic pick up, an rpm indicator and a triple tachometer
A magnetic pick up, an rpm warning unit and a master caution light
cards.explain: These three are the components of the system.

cards.question: A technician must find the rotor rpm magnetic pick up, so where is it installed?
options: Within the tail rotor gearbox
Within the main gear box
Within the rotor mast
cards.explain: It sits inside the main gear box.

cards.question: Which three components make up the mast moment monitoring system
options: A strain gauge bridge, a magnetic pick up and indicators
A strain gauge bridge, a sensor transmitting unit and indicators
A sensor transmitting unit, an rpm warning unit and indicators
cards.explain: These three are the components listed for the system.

cards.question: A strain gauge bridge is fitted for the bending moment monitoring, so where does it sit?
options: In the rotor head
In the rotor mast
In the main transmission
cards.explain: The bridge is installed in the rotor mast.

cards.question: Which kind of sensor measures the main rotor speed
options: A magnetic type one
A piezoelectric type one
A capacitive type one
cards.explain: The rotor speed pickup is a magnetic sensor.

cards.question: What is the voltage peak from the rotor speed pickup proportional to
options: The temperature of the main gear box
The movement of the interrupter
The frequency of the interrupter
cards.explain: The peak is in proportion to the interrupter frequency.

cards.question: A pilot reads the rotor rpm on the triple tachometer, so which part of the dial shows it?
options: The digital window at the foot of the dial
The large pointer N1 on the outer scale
The small pointer R on the inner scale
cards.explain: Rotor rpm is the small R pointer on the inner scale.

cards.question: The rotor rpm is shown permanently in two places in the cockpit, so which two are they?
options: The triple tachometer and the caution and advisory display
The triple tachometer and the central engine display unit
The rpm warning unit and the central engine display unit
cards.explain: Both the triple tachometer and the central engine display unit carry the rotor rpm.

cards.question: Through which unit do the speed pickup signals pass on their way to the indicators
options: The RPM warning unit
The central engine display unit
The sensor transmitting unit
cards.explain: The signals go through the rotor RPM warning unit.

cards.question: The rotor rpm falls below the operating range, so what is given to the crew?
options: A visual and an audio warning
A visual warning only
A removal of the rpm indication
cards.explain: Going outside the range either way sets off both visual and audio warning.

cards.question: Where are the sampled transmission data shown constantly
options: On the triple tachometer or on the rpm warning unit
On the analog instruments or on the mast moment indicator
On the analog instruments or on the Caution and Advisory Display
cards.explain: Either the analog indicators or the CAD carry them constantly.

cards.question: Which two transmission parameters have their own instruments showing them constantly
options: The oil temperature and the chip detection
The oil pressure and the vibration level
The oil temperature and the oil pressure
cards.explain: Transmission oil temperature and pressure are the two indicated constantly.

cards.question: A sampled transmission value goes outside its operational range, so what happens?
options: A warning appears on the respective warning unit
The parameter is taken off the display
The indication is frozen at the limit value
cards.explain: Out-of-range data produce a warning on the respective warning unit.

cards.question: What does the mast moment monitoring system measure
options: The bending moment between the rotor mast and the main transmission
The vibration between the rotor mast and the rotor head
The twisting moment between the engine and the main transmission
cards.explain: It is the bending moment between mast and main transmission.

cards.question: Through which unit does the measured mast moment reach the indicators
options: The sensor transmitting unit
The caution and advisory display
The rpm warning unit
cards.explain: The signal passes through the sensor transmitting unit.

cards.question: The maximum mast moment is exceeded in flight, so what comes with the warning light?
options: An entry in the fault memory
An aural indication
An automatic power reduction
cards.explain: An aural indication accompanies the visual one.

cards.question: How is an exceeded mast moment shown on an electronic mast moment indicator
options: By a flashing scale
By a warning light
By a red marking
cards.explain: On the electronic indicator it is a red marking; the warning light belongs to the analog one.

cards.question: A helicopter is not fitted with an EFIS, so what must be done to the mast moment indicator before each engine start?
options: It must be calibrated
It must be zeroed by the pilot
It must be tested against its warning light
cards.explain: Without an EFIS the indicator has to be calibrated before each engine start.

cards.question: A helicopter does carry an EFIS, so how is that mast moment indicator check carried out?
options: It is done by the pilot before each engine start
It is done automatically by the system
It is done by maintenance at the daily check
cards.explain: With an EFIS fitted the check is done automatically.

cards.question: A tail rotor gearbox develops a malfunction, so how will the crew learn of it?
options: By its own analog instrument
By a pointer leaving the green arc
By a caution light only
cards.explain: Gearboxes other than the main transmission are only covered by caution lights.

cards.question: Why is a main transmission fault easier to judge than a tail rotor gearbox fault
options: Both carry constant indications but only the gearbox has a light
The transmission carries only a light, the gearbox constant indications
The transmission carries constant indications, the gearbox only a light
cards.explain: Main transmission values are indicated all the time, while the other gearboxes give nothing but a caution light.

cards.question: Why can a bending load in the rotor mast be turned into a cockpit indication at all
options: Because a magnetic pick up in the mast senses the bending
Because a capacitive probe in the mast senses the bending
Because a strain gauge bridge in the mast senses the bending
cards.explain: The strain gauge bridge in the mast is what converts the bending into a signal.

cards.question: A helicopter without EFIS was started without the bending load indicator being calibrated, so what is now in doubt?
options: The aural warning of the rotor rpm
The accuracy of the mast moment indication
The supply to the strain gauge bridge
cards.explain: Without the pre-start calibration the indicated mast moment can no longer be trusted.

cards.question: Which two methods are basically used to measure the fuel quantity
options: A capacitor system and a float switch system
An ultrasonic system and a flow meter system
A capacitor system and an ultrasonic system
cards.explain: Capacitors and the ultrasonic principle are the two methods given.

cards.question: What decides the number of fuel quantity probes in a tank
options: The size and shape of the aircraft
The size and shape of that tank
The number of pumps in that tank
cards.explain: Tank size and shape set how many probes are needed.

cards.question: Which electrical component is a fuel quantity probe
options: An inductor
A resistor
A capacitor
cards.explain: Each probe is a capacitor.

cards.question: What is the material dependent factor that affects a probe's capacitance called
options: The capacitive reactance
The dielectric constant
The specific gravity
cards.explain: It is named the dielectric constant.

cards.question: A large aeroplane carries an extra fuel quantity indication outside the cockpit, so who needs it?
options: The loadmaster in the hold
The fuelling personnel
The flight crew on the walk round
cards.explain: The indication at the fuelling station is there for the fuelling personnel.

cards.question: On which aeroplanes is the ultrasonic fuel measuring principle used
options: On all of them
On smaller ones only
On larger ones only
cards.explain: The ultrasonic method is restricted to larger aeroplanes.

cards.question: How are the fuel quantity probes installed in a tank
options: Vertically, from the top down to about half depth
Vertically, from the bottom right up to the top
Horizontally, lying along the floor of the tank
cards.explain: They stand vertically and run the full depth of the tank.

cards.question: A technician lays out the probes taken from one tank, so what does he notice about them?
options: They are all of the same length
They are of different length
They are of different diameter
cards.explain: Because the tank depth varies the probes come in different lengths.

cards.question: The amount of fuel in a tank changes, so what changes at the probe?
options: Its inductance
Its capacity
Its resistance
cards.explain: The probe's capacity follows the amount of fuel.

cards.question: How are the two tubes of a fuel quantity probe arranged
options: Coaxially and electrically bonded to each other
Side by side and electrically bonded to each other
Coaxially and electrically isolated from each other
cards.explain: They sit one inside the other and are isolated, which is what makes them a capacitor.

cards.question: What is the capacitance of a fuel quantity probe
options: Its ability to generate a voltage
Its capability to store electrical energy
Its opposition to the flow of current
cards.explain: Capacitance is the ability to store electrical energy.

cards.question: On which two features of the plates does the capacitance of a probe depend
options: Their area and the thickness of them
Their length and the thickness of them
Their area and the distance between them
cards.explain: Plate area A and plate separation d are the two given.

cards.question: A small aeroplane is being fitted with a fuel quantity system, so which of the two measuring methods is open to it?
options: Either of the two methods
The one using capacitors
The one using the ultrasonic principle
cards.explain: The ultrasonic method is for larger aeroplanes only, which leaves the capacitor method.

cards.question: A tank is deep and awkwardly shaped, so what does that mean for the probes put in it?
options: One of them, laid flat at several levels
Several of them, cut to different lengths
Several of them, all cut to one length
cards.explain: Size and shape decide how many probes are needed, and because they must reach from bottom to top they end up different lengths.

cards.question: The fuel level rises past the middle of a probe, so what has happened between its two tubes?
options: The gap between the tubes has become smaller
All of the air has been replaced by fuel
Part of the air has been replaced by fuel
cards.explain: The gap is filled to the same level as the tank, so a half covered probe has fuel in part of it and air in the rest.

cards.question: Two probes in the same tank are both completely covered by fuel yet give different values, so what explains it?
options: Their plates differ in area because they differ in length
Their plates differ in spacing because they differ in fuel cover
Their plates differ in area because they differ in fuel cover
cards.explain: Probes in one tank are of different lengths, so their plate areas differ even when both are fully covered.

cards.question: The material between a probe's tubes changes from air to fuel, so what does the measuring system see?
options: A lower capacitance
A higher capacitance
An unchanged capacitance
cards.explain: Fuel in place of air raises the capacitance, because its dielectric constant is the higher one.

cards.question: Why does a capacitive probe give a different reading as the tank fills
options: Because the spacing between its tubes changes
Because the material between its tubes changes
Because the area of its tubes changes
cards.explain: Filling the tank swaps air for fuel between the tubes, and that material change alters the capacitance.

cards.question: Why does a half covered probe sit between the empty and the full capacitance value
options: Because the gap between its tubes has partly been closed up
Because only part of its plate area is still in the circuit
Because only part of the air between its tubes has been replaced
cards.explain: Fuel raises the capacitance only over the part of the probe it covers, so a half covered probe falls between the two extremes.

cards.question: Which units are used to show the fuel quantity on a large commercial aircraft
options: Units of weight
Units of volume
Units of pressure
cards.explain: On large commercial aircraft the fuel quantity is shown in units of weight.

cards.question: Which property of air and fuel the capacitance method of quantity measurement makes use of
options: Their differing electrical resistances
Their differing dielectric constants
Their differing boiling points
cards.explain: The capacitance method uses the differing dielectric constants of air and fuel.

cards.question: A bridge transformer has a centre tap and two secondary windings, so what phase relationship do the windings have to the tap?
options: Opposite
Ninety degrees apart
Identical
cards.explain: The two secondary windings are in opposite phase to the centre tap.

cards.question: How the immersion depth is measured in the fuel quantity computer system
options: By a float and an LVDT at the tank units and the compensator
By travel time of a pulse at the tank units and the compensator
By capacity changes at the tank units and the compensator
cards.explain: Immersion depth is measured by capacity changes using the tank units and the compensator.

cards.question: Which two quantities the cadensicon sensor measures separately for the computer
options: The density and the dielectric constant
The volume and the dielectric constant
The temperature and the specific gravity
cards.explain: The cadensicon measures density and dielectric constant separately.

cards.question: Which four items make up the fuel quantity indicating system that compensates fuel scatter
options: Tank units, a computer, a densitometer and a water detector
Tank units, a computer, a cadensicon and a compensator
Tank units, a totaliser, a repeater and a compensator
cards.explain: The system has tank units, a fuel quantity indicating computer, a cadensicon sensor and a compensator.

cards.question: A technician looks for the compensator inside a fuel tank, so where in the tank is it installed?
options: At about mid height
Near the lowest point
Near the highest point
cards.explain: The compensators are installed near to the lowest point of the tanks.

cards.question: Why the amount of fuel carried is indicated in units of weight
options: The energy available from the fuel depends on weight
The energy available from the fuel depends on volume
The tank capacity is certified in terms of weight
cards.explain: The energy present in the form of fuel is dependent on weight, so weight is indicated.

cards.question: What makes a direct weight indication of the fuel necessary on a large commercial aircraft
options: Fuel can be half the take-off weight and the approved weights need it
Fuel is always loaded by volume and the tank gauges are marked in litres only
Fuel density is constant so the weight can be read straight from the volume
cards.explain: Fuel can be up to one half of take-off weight, so direct weight indication is needed for the approved take-off and landing weights.

cards.question: The same number of litres of fuel is loaded on a very cold day and on a very hot day, so what differs between the two loads?
options: The weight on board
The capacity of the empty tank
The dielectric constant of the fuel
cards.explain: Volume and specific gravity change with temperature, so the same number of litres can differ by several tonnes.

cards.question: The fuel level in a tank alters, so what does the multi-tubular surface condenser in it do?
options: It changes its resistance
It changes its excitation frequency
It changes its capacity
cards.explain: The condenser changes its capacity depending on the level of fuel in the tank.

cards.question: What the total capacity of the tank condenser is made up of
options: The empty tank capacity minus the change from fuel displacing air
The empty tank capacity plus the change from fuel displacing air
The change from fuel displacing air on its own
cards.explain: Total capacity is the empty tank capacity plus the capacity change due to the displacement of air between the plates.

cards.question: What happens to the capacitance of a tank sensor as the tank fills with fuel
options: It decreases
It increases
It stays constant
cards.explain: Fuel has a dielectric strength more than twice that of air, so sensor capacitance rises with fuel content.

cards.question: A tank sensor has changed its capacitance as the tank filled, so where is that change used?
options: In a bridge circuit that gives an amplified signal
In a resolver circuit that gives a shaft angle output
In a chopper circuit that gives a pulse train output
cards.explain: The change in capacitance is used in a bridge circuit to provide an amplified signal.

cards.question: What the amplified signal from the capacitance bridge acts on
options: The pointer or the digital display
The shutoff valve in the refuelling gallery line
The excitation winding of the tank unit sensor
cards.explain: The amplified signal rotates the pointer or actuates the digital display in the indicator.

cards.question: What condition exists when the tank unit capacitance and the reference condenser capacitance are equal
options: No current runs through the instrument
Maximum current runs through the instrument
A current runs that drives the pointer to full
cards.explain: With equal capacitances the two currents compensate each other and nothing flows through the instrument.

cards.question: What is true of the two points across which the instrument is connected when the bridge is balanced
options: They are at the supply potential
They are at opposite electrical potential
They are at the same electrical potential
cards.explain: At balance the two points have the same electrical potential, so no current flows.

cards.question: What the position of the potentiometer arm represents once the bridge has been rebalanced
options: The supply voltage applied to the bridge
The ratio of the two capacitance values
The sum of the two capacitance readings
cards.explain: The potentiometer arm position indicates the ratio of the two capacitance values.

cards.question: How the capacitive bridge of a fuel quantity indicator is rebalanced in service
options: Automatically, by amplifying the difference signal
Automatically, by switching in reference condensers
Manually, by the crew turning a trimming knob
cards.explain: Fuel quantity capacitive bridges are balanced automatically by amplifying the difference signal.

cards.question: The amplifier of a capacitive fuel gauge puts out a voltage, so what does that voltage drive?
options: A motor that turns the potentiometer
A solenoid that trips the warning flag
A heater that trims the reference condenser
cards.explain: The amplifier output voltage drives a motor which turns the potentiometer.

cards.question: Fuel is being burned off in flight and the gauge is following it down, so what brings the rebalancing motor to rest at each new reading?
options: The amplifier output reaching its limit
The difference signal falling to zero
The potentiometer reaching its end stop
cards.explain: The motor stops when the difference signal is zero.

cards.question: How the bridge turns a change of tank capacitance into something the indicator can show
options: The secondary winding phase is taken as the indication
The instrument current is taken straight as the indication
The rebalanced potentiometer position is indicated
cards.explain: The bridge is rebalanced by the motor-driven potentiometer, and the motor or potentiometer position is what is indicated.

cards.question: Why the relationship between dielectric constant and density has to be corrected
options: It varies with the fuel consistency of each country
It varies with the age of the tank units in the tank
It varies with the altitude the aircraft is flown at
cards.explain: The ratio of K to D varies in accordance with fuel consistency in individual countries.

cards.question: How the dielectric constant is obtained inside a cadensicon sensor
options: From the depth of immersion of a float
From the capacity change of a condenser
From the travel time of an ultrasonic pulse
cards.explain: K is calculated from the capacity change of a condenser.

cards.question: How the density is obtained inside a cadensicon sensor
options: By a condenser whose capacity changes with the fuel
By a thermistor bridge sensing the fuel temperature
By a cardanically suspended float of fixed weight
cards.explain: D is found mechanically by a cardanically suspended float of predetermined weight.

cards.question: The cadensicon float has sunk to a certain depth in the fuel, so how is that depth turned into a signal for the computer?
options: By a synchro resolver
By a strain gauge
By an LVDT
cards.explain: The depth of immersion is measured by an LVDT and sent to the computer.

cards.question: How density is found in systems that damp a mass instead of floating one
options: From the force needed to hold the damped mass still
From the ratio of oscillations added to those removed
From the time the damped mass takes to come to rest
cards.explain: In those systems the ratio of oscillations added to oscillations removed determines density.

cards.question: What the fuel quantity indicating computer works out from the probes it monitors
options: The mass of fuel in the related tank
The volume of fuel in the related tank
The density of fuel in the related tank
cards.explain: The computer uses signal conditioning on the probe signals to calculate the volume of fuel in the related tank.

cards.question: When the cadensicon sensor takes its measurements of K and D
options: Only when the tank is nearly empty
As fuel enters the tank
Only once the engines have been started
cards.explain: The cadensicon measures K and D separately as fuel enters the tank.

cards.question: In what form the cadensicon delivers its two outputs to the computer
options: Both as electrical signals
One electrical and one pneumatic
Both as mechanical movements
cards.explain: Outputs K and D are both electrical signals.

cards.question: A cadensicon sensor measures two properties of the fuel, so which one of them is sensed mechanically?
options: The temperature
The dielectric constant
The density
cards.explain: K is measured electrically only while D is measured mechanically by a float.

cards.question: What the fuel scatter effect is
options: The capacitance of a probe drifts as the probe gets older
The K to D relationship alters as the fuel temperature changes
The K to D relationship is not constant between fuel samples
cards.explain: Fuel scatter is the phenomenon that the relationship of K to D between different fuel samples is not constant.

cards.question: The fuel in a tank warms up over a long flight, so what happens to the relationship between K and D?
options: It is pulled back onto the average law
It is not influenced by temperature
It changes in step with the fuel density
cards.explain: A change in temperature will not influence this relationship.

cards.question: Water has collected between the plates of a capacitance probe, so how does the probe capacitance compare with the same probe covered in fuel?
options: The same
Slightly lower
Much higher
cards.explain: Water is given a far larger dielectric constant than fuel, and the capacitance rises with the dielectric constant of whatever fills the probe.

cards.question: Water lying in a tank gives a far greater capacitance than fuel does, so how would the quantity indication be affected?
options: It would read above the fuel actually present
It would read below the fuel actually present
It would stay at the correct reading
cards.explain: The capacitance follows the dielectric constant of what fills the probe, and water's is far above that of fuel, so the gauge reads more fuel than is there.

cards.question: Why the capacity of a tank condenser is compared with its capacity when the tank is empty
options: The difference corresponds to the quantity of fuel present
The difference corresponds to the dielectric constant of the fuel
The difference corresponds to the temperature of the fuel
cards.explain: The capacity above the empty tank value is the part caused by fuel, and that difference corresponds to the fuel quantity.

cards.question: What is gained by leaving the tank unit as the only variable in the bridge
options: A lower supply current to the bridge
A faster response of the indication
Greater precision of the indication
cards.explain: Having only the tank unit variable increases indicator precision.

cards.question: The aircraft is being refuelled and the level in a tank is rising, so what is happening at the master indicator?
options: Compensator current rises and the indication holds steady
Tank unit current falls and the indication moves downscale
Tank unit current rises and the indication moves upscale
cards.explain: A rising level raises the tank unit capacitance and current, and the quantity indicator moves upscale.

cards.question: Why the indicator runs downscale when the fuel quantity test switch is operated
options: The supply to the rebalancing motor is reversed
The compensator current that normally drives it to full is missing
The tank unit current that normally drives it to full is missing
cards.explain: Operating the test switch removes the tank unit current that normally moves the indicator towards FULL, so it runs downscale.

cards.question: A coaxial cable to one tank unit has broken so that no tank unit current reaches its master indicator, so what will that indicator do?
options: Freeze at the last reading
Run upscale to full
Run downscale
cards.explain: A missing tank unit current is what the test switch creates, and it drives the indicator downscale.

cards.question: The rebalancing motor of a capacitive gauge has just run to a stop, so what is true of the two bridge currents at that moment?
options: They are equal
They are both at zero
They are in opposite phase
cards.explain: The motor runs until the two currents are equal, and that is where it stops.

cards.question: The master indicator already shows the figure it has worked out, so how do the repeater and the fuel summation unit come to show the same?
options: The computed value is sent to them over the compensator line
The tank unit current is sent to them over the coaxial cable
The synchronising voltage is sent to them from the totaliser
cards.explain: The value shown on the master indicator is transmitted in a further circuit via the compensator line to the repeater and the fuel summation unit.

cards.question: How the built-in test of the computerised system differs from the test started by the flight deck switch
options: One runs automatically and codes faults, the other tests the displays
One runs automatically and tests the displays, the other codes faults
One tests the displays, the other codes faults found on the ground only
cards.explain: The built-in test runs automatically and shows any fault as an error code, while the FQ test switch starts a display test of all indicators.

cards.question: A computerised fuel quantity indicator is showing an error code instead of a quantity, so which of the computer circuits produced it?
options: The one running the automatic system check
The one feeding the repeater and the summation unit
The one sending the signal out to the tank units
cards.explain: The error code comes from the separate circuit that runs the automatic system check by built-in test.

cards.question: A float sinks further in one fuel sample than in another of the same temperature, so what does that tell the computer?
options: That the two samples differ in volume
That the two samples differ in density
That the two samples differ in dielectric constant
cards.explain: The float of predetermined weight submerges in accordance with the density, so a deeper float means a different density.

cards.question: Refuelling has to stop before a tank overflows, so what is built into the fuel quantity computer system for this?
options: A totaliser that sums all of the master systems
A preselection of the wanted load with a shutoff
A trimming condenser at the cockpit indicator
cards.explain: The system integrates a preselection of the desired volume together with a shutoff on reaching it or shortly before overflowing.

cards.question: Why the aircraft attitude matters to the preselection and shutoff function
options: The density measured by the float depends on aircraft position
The dielectric constant of the fuel depends on aircraft position
The point at which a tank overflows depends on aircraft position
cards.explain: Shutoff occurs on reaching the preselected value or shortly before overflowing, which depends on aircraft position.

cards.question: What the computer derives from the cadensicon and compensator data it monitors
options: The density of the fuel in the tanks
The temperature of the fuel in the tanks
The volume of the fuel in the tanks
cards.explain: Cadensicon and compensator data are used to calculate the density of the fuel in the tanks.

cards.question: The probes alone can only tell the computer how much space the fuel fills, so what else must it have before a figure in kilograms can be shown?
options: The temperature of the fuel
The usable capacity of the tank
The density of the fuel
cards.explain: The computer needs both the volume and the fuel density before it can calculate the fuel mass.

cards.question: The outer tanks still hold fuel from the previous flight when fresh fuel is loaded, so how does the computer handle the mixture?
options: It ignores the old fuel until that tank has been emptied
It calculates a mean value from the old and the new fuel
It applies the values of the fresh fuel to both quantities
cards.explain: The computer can calculate a mean value from the remaining fuel and the replenished fuel.

cards.question: Why fuel taken on at two different airports can upset the quantity indication unless the computer allows for it
options: The two loads can have different fuel temperatures
The two loads can have different K to D values
The two loads can have different tank unit capacitances
cards.explain: Fuel consistency differs between countries, so the remaining and replenished fuel can have different K to D values that the computer has to average.

cards.question: Which kind of signal the tank units of this liquid level metering system transmit
options: An ultrasonic signal
A light pulse
A radio frequency signal
cards.explain: The tank units transmit an ultrasonic signal.

cards.question: A tank of an ultrasonic system is opened for inspection, so how many tank units will be found in it?
options: A single unit
Numerous units
Exactly two units
cards.explain: Each tank contains numerous tank units.

cards.question: A technician surveys an ultrasonic fuel tank installation, so how many densitometers will each tank have?
options: One
One for every tank unit
Two
cards.explain: Each fuel tank has one densitometer.

cards.question: Where the water detectors are fitted
options: At the highest point of each fuel tank
At the low point in each fuel tank
In the refuelling gallery pipework
cards.explain: Water detectors are at the low point in each fuel tank.

cards.question: Which kind of quantity measuring systems the GF-2 fuel tester is used on
options: Float operated gauging systems
Capacitance measuring systems
Ultrasonic measuring systems
cards.explain: The tester is used for capacitance measuring systems for fuel and oil.

cards.question: Which three functions the tester for capacitance quantity systems provides
options: Measuring capacities, simulating capacities and measuring contact resistances
Measuring resistances, simulating voltages and measuring tank unit currents
Measuring capacities, simulating densities and measuring insulation resistances
cards.explain: The tester measures capacities, simulates capacities and measures contact resistances.

cards.question: Where the signal sent out by an ultrasonic tank unit is reflected
options: At the wall of the stillwell tube
At the bottom of the tank sump
At the surface of the liquid
cards.explain: The signal is reflected at the surface of the liquid.

cards.question: What picks up the echo in an ultrasonic quantity metering system
options: The compensator near the tank bottom
A separate receiver at the tank top
The tank unit that sent the signal
cards.explain: The same tank unit that transmits also receives the echo.

cards.question: A computer has received the echo from an ultrasonic tank unit, so what does it use to find the liquid level?
options: The running time of the signal
The strength of the returned echo
The frequency shift of the returned echo
cards.explain: The computer calculates the liquid level from the running time of the signal.

cards.question: What the fuel quantity processor unit measures in order to find the fuel height
options: The frequency of the returned pulse
The travel time of the pulse
The strength of the returned pulse
cards.explain: The processor unit measures the travel time of the pulse and uses it to find the fuel height.

cards.question: Through what the sonic pulse travels on its way to the fuel surface
options: The wall of the tank unit
The air space above the fuel
The fuel in the stillwell
cards.explain: The pulse goes through the fuel in the stillwell to the fuel surface and back to the receiver.

cards.question: Some tank units also carry calibration targets, so what does the processor unit get from the pulses that come back off them?
options: The velocity of sound in the fuel
The density of the fuel in the tank
The depth of water in the tank sump
cards.explain: Pulses reflected from the targets are used to measure the velocity of sound in the fuel.

cards.question: Which kind of transducer a densitometer uses
options: A vibrating cylinder
A capacitive condenser
A cardanically suspended float
cards.explain: Densitometers use a vibrating cylinder transducer.

cards.question: A densitometer output frequency is being read off, so what is that frequency proportional to?
options: The fuel temperature
The fuel height
The fuel density
cards.explain: The frequency of the vibrations is proportional to the fuel density.

cards.question: How a water detector shows that water is lying in the bottom of a tank
options: Its float sinks in the water and drives a transformer
Its pulse is absorbed so that no echo returns at all
Its pulse reflects off the boundary with the fuel
cards.explain: If water is present the pulse reflects off the interface between the water and the fuel.

cards.question: A technician is told the water detectors work in the same way as the tank units, so what kind of devices are they?
options: Ultrasonic devices
Resistive devices
Capacitive devices
cards.explain: The water detectors are ultrasonic devices like the tank units.

cards.question: Which part of the test equipment must be kept clear of the airframe during a capacitance check
options: The connector of the tank unit
The casing of the tester
The shielding of the coaxial cable
cards.explain: The tester casing must never come into contact with the airframe.

cards.question: Which property of the fuel the capacitance of a tank unit responds to, unlike an ultrasonic tank unit
options: Its dielectric constant
Its temperature in flight
Its density in the tank
cards.explain: Capacitive measurement works from the differing dielectric constants, while the ultrasonic unit works from a reflected signal.

cards.question: An ultrasonic system has to display a fuel weight, so which two measurements must the processor unit bring together?
options: The fuel density and the velocity of sound
The fuel height and the fuel temperature
The fuel height and the fuel density
cards.explain: Height comes from the tank units and density from the densitometer, and the FQPU calculates the fuel weight from them.

cards.question: How the ultrasonic system obtains the density it needs, compared with a capacitive cadensicon system
options: From a float and a condenser instead of a vibrating cylinder
From the pulse travel time instead of a vibrating cylinder
From a vibrating cylinder instead of a float and a condenser
cards.explain: The ultrasonic system gets density from a vibrating cylinder densitometer, whereas the cadensicon gets it from a float with K from a condenser.

cards.question: A densitometer in one tank of an ultrasonic system has failed, so which calculation is lost first?
options: The water level in that tank
The fuel height in that tank
The fuel weight for that tank
cards.explain: Height still comes from the tank unit, but without the density from the densitometer the processor unit cannot work out that tank's fuel weight.

cards.question: A capacitance quantity system has to be checked on the ground with the tanks drained, so what does the tester let the technician do instead of wetting the probes?
options: Measure the fuel density
Simulate the capacities
Measure the contact resistances
cards.explain: The tester can simulate capacities as well as measure them.

cards.question: A tank unit reads correctly on the tester but the cockpit indication is still wrong, so which further tester function would be used on the wiring?
options: Measuring the tank unit currents
Simulating the probe capacities
Measuring contact resistances
cards.explain: Besides measuring and simulating capacities the tester measures contact resistances, which is what a wiring check needs.
